grades.quote: A struct cpu (1971) holds a pointer to the proc structure of the process currently running on that CPU (if any), saved registers for the CPU’s scheduler thread, and the count of nested spinlocks needed to manage interrupt disabling.
grades.reason: Provides related per-CPU interrupt-disable bookkeeping, but not the reason spinlocks require interrupts disabled.

grades.quote: Suppose sys_pause holds tickslock, and its CPU is interrupted by a timer interrupt. clockintr would try to acquire tickslock, see it was held, and wait for it to be released. In this situation, tickslock will never be released: only sys_pause can release it, but sys_pause will not continue running until clockintr returns.
grades.reason: Directly explains that disabling interrupts prevents same-CPU deadlock when an interrupt handler attempts to acquire a lock held by interrupted code.
